business: Marlpit — a nineteen-person mineral-paint maker at a mill in Wiltshire, selling limewash, silicate, clay distemper and lime-casein paints in thirty-six colours to owners of solid-wall and historic buildings, to conservation officers specifying for listed work, and to the builders who apply it. Its argument is that a solid wall manages moisture by letting it move, and that modern vinyl emulsion is a film formulated not to let water vapour through. Its commercial first step is four sample pots for £22, sold on the explicit basis that no screen and no printed card is good enough to choose a colour from.
businessKind: retail and commerce with a large catalogue
directionLabel: Painted — the site is made of the product
